items.stem: What does putting `[EntityProperty]` on a property do?

options.text: Runs code immediately when that line is reached
Attaches metadata that the engine reads at runtime to tag the field for change detection
Creates a new database column
Throws an exception if the value is null

items.explanation: Attributes are passive metadata; the engine reads [EntityProperty] via reflection and tracks that field for change detection.

misconceptions.a: Attributes don't execute where they sit — they're read later by a framework.

items.stem: In general .NET terms, what is an attribute?

options.text: A bracketed annotation that attaches metadata, read by tooling/frameworks (often via reflection)
A special kind of loop
A method that must return void
A way to inherit from two base classes

items.explanation: Attributes attach declarative metadata to code elements; frameworks read them at runtime to decide behavior.

items.stem: In the Synnduit POCO contract, which statement is correct?

options.text: The attributes are documentation only and have no effect
The engine reads the attributes by reflection and uses them to drive change detection, dedup, and mapping
The attributes generate the destination's SQL schema
The attributes are executed top-to-bottom like statements

items.explanation: Synnduit reads the POCO's attributes at runtime to learn how to handle the entity — they're functional metadata, not decoration.

misconceptions.a: They are functional — omitting [EntityProperty], for instance, stops a field being tracked.

items.stem: Explain why forgetting `[EntityProperty]` on a field is a 'silent' bug, in terms of what attributes are.
rubric: Attributes are runtime metadata, not compiled instructions — omitting one is not a compile error
Without [EntityProperty] the engine simply never tracks that field, so changes go undetected with no error
items.sampleAnswer: Because attributes are passive metadata the engine reads at runtime, leaving one off isn't a compile error. The code builds fine; the engine just never learns to track that field, so its changes are silently ignored.

items.stem: How does the Synnduit engine actually discover that a property is marked `[DuplicationKey]`?

options.text: It reads the attribute via reflection at runtime
The attribute runs code that registers itself when the class loads
The compiler turns it into a method call
It is listed in appsettings.json

items.explanation: Attributes are metadata; frameworks like Synnduit inspect them with reflection to decide behavior — here, which field drives dedup.

misconceptions.b: Attributes don't execute themselves; something else reads them later.

items.stem: On Staff.cs, EmployeeId carries both `[EntityProperty]` and `[DuplicationKey]`. Is stacking multiple attributes on one member allowed?

options.text: Yes — a member can carry multiple attributes, and the engine reads each
No — only one attribute per member is permitted
Only if they are written on separate lines
Only on classes, never on properties

items.explanation: A code element can have many attributes; here EmployeeId is both tracked for change detection and used as the dedup key.

misconceptions.b: Multiple attributes per member are fine and common in the POCO contract.
